title: Error provenance ledger and signal normalizer for tracing + metrics pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an "error provenance ledger" and a lightweight "signal normalizer" to unify how timeouts, overload, model-level errors, and HTTP/gRPC codes are represented across tracing hooks, metrics, and logs. The goal is a single canonical attribution field (error_provenance) that powers a new Error Provenance Ledger dashboard and upstream normalization in the metrics/log pipeline so downstream SLOs, cost-analysis, and oncall workflows operate on consistent signals.

Context: Over the last year we've had multiple dashboards and runbooks that disagree about root causes because teams surface errors differently (e.g., runtime timeouts vs. proxy timeouts vs. model rejection vs. overloaded queue). This causes noisy pager churn and makes capacity decisions harder. The ledger will codify attribution rules and transformations applied at ingestion (metrics + logs) and at trace capture time.

Scope:
- Instrument tracing hooks to emit standardized attributes: error_provenance, error_type, error_subtype, origin_service, model_variant, kernel_profile.
- Add a signal normalizer stage in the metrics/log pipeline (Kafka -> Enrichment -> OLAP) that maps legacy fields (http_status, grpc_code, model_exit_code, vm_exit_reason, kv_cache_status) into error_provenance values with evidence tags.
- Ship a dashboard (Error Provenance Ledger) that supports multi-dimensional slices (service, route, model, host-type, time-window) and links into trace samples and GitHub PRs.
- Update the oncall runbook with new triage flow and rollback steps for model overload signals.

Design details (high level):
1) Tracing hook changes: Add an enrichment step in trace-agent that populates: error_provenance (enum), error_reason (free text), error_confidence (0-1), model_variant, kernel_hint. error_provenance enums: timeout_client, timeout_runtime, overload_queue, overload_gpu, model_rejection, model_nan, http_4xx, http_5xx, grpc_retryable, grpc_fatal, network_error, dependency_failure, unknown. The hook should prefer deterministic signals (e.g., dispatcher timeout header beats gRPC code) and attach evidence array (string list).

2) Metrics/log normalization: Introduce a lightweight normalization microservice (signal-normalizer) that consumes raw telemetry topic and emits normalized messages to telemetry-enriched topic. Normalizer rules are config-driven (yaml) to allow quick edits during incidents. Normalizer outputs include: normalized_error_provenance, normalized_tags, original_payload_ref. Normalizer will run in dedicated autoscaled pods with backpressure to avoid cascading failures.

3) Dashboard spec: Error Provenance Ledger with panels:
- Provenance distribution (stacked area) by service and model_variant
- Top contributing traces for each provenance type (linked to Trace Viewer)
- Latency P99 and error_provenance correlation scatter (shows overload vs timeout clusters)
- SLO exposure table (routes with >=1% error_provenance=overload_queue)
- Evidence explorer (shows raw evidence snippets that produced the mapping)

4) Backwards compatibility: Keep legacy http_status/grpc_code counters and add mapped counters (e.g., errors_by_provenance). Migration plan will keep both for 6 weeks and then remove deprecated dashboards.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): implement trace-agent enrichment and local normalizer, unit tests for mapping rules (2w).
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy normalizer to telemetry-canary, enable for 5% of traffic for non-critical services (2w).
- Phase 2 (ramp): 50% then 100% over 2 weeks, monitor SLOs and Kafka lag.
- Phase 3 (dashboard + runbook): publish Ledger dashboard and update runbook + run an oncall playbook drill (1w).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for rule engine and trace enrichment.
- Integration tests: end-to-end from request -> trace -> normalizer -> OLAP shows mapped provenance.
- Synthetic scenarios: generate timeouts at different layers, overload the queue, and trigger model rejection codes to validate evidence mapping.
- Load test normalizer service with 10k msgs/sec to ensure 99th percentile processing <50ms.

Rollbacks and safety: normalizer supports passthrough mode (emit original payload without mapping) and a kill-switch that switches consumers back to raw topic. Tracing hooks emit both legacy attributes and new attributes to avoid losing data.

Observability & metrics for the feature itself: monitor normalizer CPU, latency_p99, Kafka consumer lag, mapping_rate, unmapped_rate, and a signal_normalizer_alert when unmapped_rate > 0.5% for more than 10m.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misclassification causes bad oncall actions. Mitigation: low-confidence tags + UI shows evidence; map rules are config-driven and behind a feature flag.
- Risk: normalizer adds latency to metrics pipeline. Mitigation: fast-path sampling and autoscale.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks emit error_provenance, error_reason and evidence attributes for 95% of error events in canary services.
Signal normalizer transforms legacy telemetry into normalized_error_provenance for at least 99% of messages with unmapped_rate < 0.5% in steady state.
Error Provenance Ledger dashboard displays provenance distribution, top traces, and SLO exposure and links to trace samples.
Runbook updated and oncall drill performed with postmortem documenting any mismatches and mapping fixes.
Migration: legacy counters kept for 6 weeks; after which all internal dashboards point to normalized counters without regressions in alerting.
Performance: normalizer handles target throughput in load tests with p99 latency < 50ms and CPU/memory within expected budgets.

2026-02-22 - Daniel Kim: Reviewed design; recommended adding error_confidence field and evidence snippets to help triage. Also proposed config-driven rule YAML for quick fixes.
2026-02-25 - Mariana Lopez (SRE): Suggested a canary plan that starts with background traffic and non-prod models. Added requirement to preserve legacy counters for 6 weeks.

2026-03-02 - Daniel Kim: Implemented trace-agent enrichment prototype. Evidence array includes dispatcher headers and gRPC status. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-agent/pull/482 (WIP).
2026-03-05 - Design review with PM: Agreed on dashboard panels and added 'evidence explorer' to help classification debugging. PM asked for links to recent incidents for examples.

2026-03-08 - Integration update: Signal normalizer local runner processes mappings end-to-end. Running mapping unit tests; unmapped cases logged to a review queue. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-normalizer/pull/13.

2026-03-10 - Daniel Kim: Kickoff canary next week targeting 5% traffic for non-critical services. Added monitoring alerts for unmapped_rate and kafka lag. Assigned follow-ups: ENG-712346 (rule remediation dashboard) and ENG-712347 (runbook drill planning).
